servers:
  - url: https://api.uitrace.dev/v1
    description: Production server
  - url: https://staging-api.uitrace.dev/v1
    description: Staging server
  - url: http://localhost:8000/v1
    description: Development server

security:
  - BearerAuth: []
  - OAuth2: []

components:
  securitySchemes:
    BearerAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      bearerFormat: JWT
    OAuth2:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.uitrace.dev/oauth/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://auth.uitrace.dev/oauth/token
          scopes:
            read: Read access to projects and scripts
            write: Write access to projects and scripts
            admin: Administrative access

  schemas:
    User:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - email
        - username
        - role
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          example: "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
        email:
          type: string
          format: email
          example: "user@example.com"
        username:
          type: string
          minLength: 3
          maxLength: 50
          example: "testuser"
        role:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/UserRole'
        oauthProvider:
          type: string
          enum: [google, github, microsoft, null]
          nullable: true
        isActive:
          type: boolean
          default: true
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        lastLogin:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true

    UserRole:
      type: string
      enum: [admin, tester, viewer]

    Team:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - name
        - createdBy
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "QA Team"
        description:
          type: string
          example: "Main quality assurance team"
        createdBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        memberCount:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
          example: 5

    Project:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - name
        - teamId
        - createdBy
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "E-commerce Test Suite"
        description:
          type: string
          example: "Comprehensive e-commerce testing scripts"
        teamId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        createdBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        isActive:
          type: boolean
          default: true
        dataRetentionMonths:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 60
          default: 12
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        scriptCount:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
          example: 25

    TestScript:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - projectId
        - name
        - version
        - status
        - scriptContent
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        projectId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "Login Test Flow"
        description:
          type: string
          example: "User login and navigation test"
        version:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          example: 3
        status:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScriptStatus'
        scriptContent:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestStep'
        lockedBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          nullable: true
        lockedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
        createdBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    ScriptStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [draft, ready, archived]

    TestStep:
      type: object
      required:
        - stepId
        - action
        - selectors
        - timeoutSeconds
      properties:
        stepId:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          example: 1
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
          example: "Navigate to login page"
        action:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/StepAction'
        value:
          type: string
          example: "https://example.com/login"
        expectedValue:
          type: string
          nullable: true
        timeoutSeconds:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 300
          default: 20
        selectors:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ElementSelector'
          minItems: 1
          maxItems: 5

    StepAction:
      type: string
      enum: [navigate, click, type, assert_text, assert_url, screenshot, wait]

    ElementSelector:
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - value
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [id, css, xpath, name]
        value:
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          example: "#login-button"

    TestDataFile:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - projectId
        - name
        - fileType
        - columnHeaders
        - rowCount
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        projectId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "user_data.csv"
        description:
          type: string
          example: "Test user data for login scenarios"
        fileType:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/DataFileType'
        filePath:
          type: string
          readOnly: true
        fileSize:
          type: integer
          format: int64
          example: 10240
        columnHeaders:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ColumnHeader'
        rowCount:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          example: 100
        createdBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    DataFileType:
      type: string
      enum: [csv, excel]

    ColumnHeader:
      type: object
      required:
        - name
        - type
      properties:
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "username"
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [string, number, boolean, date]
        required:
          type: boolean
          default: false

    TestExecution:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - scriptId
        - projectId
        - browserType
        - executionMode
        - status
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        scriptId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        projectId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        executionName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
          example: "Daily Regression Test"
        browserType:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BrowserType'
        executionMode:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ExecutionMode'
        status:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ExecutionStatus'
        startedBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        startedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        completedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
        totalDurationMs:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
        totalSteps:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
        successfulSteps:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true
        failedSteps:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true

    BrowserType:
      type: string
      enum: [chrome, firefox, edge, safari]

    ExecutionMode:
      type: string
      enum: [sequential, parallel, data_driven]

    ExecutionStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled]

    TestCase:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - executionId
        - dataRowIndex
        - status
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        executionId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        dataRowIndex:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
        status:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/CaseStatus'
        startedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        completedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
        durationMs:
          type: integer
          readOnly: true

    CaseStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [pending, running, completed, failed, skipped]

    VisualBaseline:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - scriptId
        - stepIndex
        - baselineName
        - screenshotPath
        - similarityThreshold
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        scriptId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        stepIndex:
          type: integer
          minimum: 0
        baselineName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 100
        screenshotPath:
          type: string
          readOnly: true
        similarityThreshold:
          type: number
          minimum: 0.0
          maximum: 1.0
          default: 0.98
        createdBy:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    VisualComparison:
      type: object
      required:
        - id
        - baselineId
        - similarityScore
        - differencePercentage
        - comparisonStatus
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        baselineId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        testStepId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        currentScreenshotPath:
          type: string
          readOnly: true
        similarityScore:
          type: number
          minimum: 0.0
          maximum: 1.0
          example: 0.9542
        differencePercentage:
          type: number
          minimum: 0.0
          maximum: 100.0
          example: 4.58
        comparisonStatus:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/ComparisonStatus'
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    ComparisonStatus:
      type: string
      enum: [pending, passed, failed, error]

    ErrorResponse:
      type: object
      required:
        - error
        - message
        - timestamp
      properties:
        error:
          type: string
          example: "VALIDATION_ERROR"
        message:
          type: string
          example: "Invalid email format"
        details:
          type: object
        timestamp:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    PaginatedResponse:
      type: object
      required:
        - data
        - pagination
      properties:
        data:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
        pagination:
          type: object
          required:
            - page
            - limit
            - total
            - totalPages
          properties:
            page:
              type: integer
              minimum: 1
            limit:
              type: integer
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 100
            total:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0
            totalPages:
              type: integer
              minimum: 0

paths:
  /auth/login:
    post:
      summary: User login
      tags: [Authentication]
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [email, password]
              properties:
                email:
                  type: string
                  format: email
                password:
                  type: string
                  minLength: 8
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Login successful
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  accessToken:
                    type: string
                  refreshToken:
                    type: string
                  user:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'
        '401':
          description: Invalid credentials
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'

  /auth/oauth/{provider}:
    get:
      summary: OAuth2 authorization
      tags: [Authentication]
      security: []
      parameters:
        - name: provider
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [google, github, microsoft]
      responses:
        '302':
          description: Redirect to provider

  /auth/refresh:
    post:
      summary: Refresh access token
      tags: [Authentication]
      security: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [refreshToken]
              properties:
                refreshToken:
                  type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Token refreshed
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  accessToken:
                    type: string
        '401':
          description: Invalid refresh token

  /users/profile:
    get:
      summary: Get user profile
      tags: [Users]
      responses:
        '200':
          description: User profile retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/User'

  /teams:
    get:
      summary: Get user teams
      tags: [Teams]
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Teams retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaginatedResponse'
        '401':
          description: Unauthorized

    post:
      summary: Create team
      tags: [Teams]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name]
              properties:
                name:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                description:
                  type: string
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Team created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Team'

  /projects:
    get:
      summary: Get projects
      tags: [Projects]
      parameters:
        - name: teamId
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
        - name: page
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 1
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
            maximum: 100
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Projects retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaginatedResponse'

    post:
      summary: Create project
      tags: [Projects]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name, teamId]
              properties:
                name:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                description:
                  type: string
                teamId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
                dataRetentionMonths:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                  maximum: 60
                  default: 12
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Project created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Project'

  /projects/{projectId}/scripts:
    get:
      summary: Get project scripts
      tags: [Scripts]
      parameters:
        - name: projectId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
        - name: page
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 1
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
            maximum: 100
        - name: status
          in: query
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScriptStatus'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Scripts retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaginatedResponse'

    post:
      summary: Create test script
      tags: [Scripts]
      parameters:
        - name: projectId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [name, scriptContent]
              properties:
                name:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                description:
                  type: string
                scriptContent:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestStep'
                status:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScriptStatus'
                  default: draft
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Script created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestScript'

  /projects/{projectId}/data:
    post:
      summary: Upload test data file
      tags: [Data]
      parameters:
        - name: projectId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [file, name]
              properties:
                file:
                  type: string
                  format: binary
                name:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                description:
                  type: string
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Data file uploaded
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestDataFile'

  /executions:
    post:
      summary: Start test execution
      tags: [Executions]
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [scriptId, browserType]
              properties:
                scriptId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
                executionName:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                browserType:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/BrowserType'
                executionMode:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/ExecutionMode'
                  default: sequential
                dataFileId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Execution started
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestExecution'

    get:
      summary: Get executions
      tags: [Executions]
      parameters:
        - name: projectId
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
        - name: status
          in: query
          schema:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ExecutionStatus'
        - name: page
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 1
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
            maximum: 100
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Executions retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaginatedResponse'

  /executions/{executionId}:
    get:
      summary: Get execution details
      tags: [Executions]
      parameters:
        - name: executionId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Execution details retrieved
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/TestExecution'

    delete:
      summary: Cancel execution
      tags: [Executions]
      parameters:
        - name: executionId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Execution cancelled

  /executions/{executionId}/visual-baselines:
    post:
      summary: Create visual baseline
      tags: [Visual Testing]
      parameters:
        - name: executionId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [stepIndex, baselineName, screenshotFile]
              properties:
                stepIndex:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 0
                baselineName:
                  type: string
                  maxLength: 100
                screenshotFile:
                  type: string
                  format: binary
                similarityThreshold:
                  type: number
                  minimum: 0.0
                  maximum: 1.0
                  default: 0.98
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Visual baseline created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/VisualBaseline'

tags:
  - name: Authentication
    description: User authentication and authorization
  - name: Users
    description: User profile management
  - name: Teams
    description: Team management and collaboration
  - name: Projects
    description: Project management and configuration
  - name: Scripts
    description: Test script creation and management
  - name: Data
    description: Test data file management
  - name: Executions
    description: Test execution monitoring and control
  - name: Visual Testing
    description: Visual baseline and comparison management

input.content:
# Quick Start Guide: UITrace Platform

**Purpose**: Get started with UITrace UI automation testing platform
**Created**: 2025-11-27
**Target Audience**: QA engineers, developers, and testers new to UITrace

## Prerequisites

### System Requirements
- **Desktop Client**: Windows 10+, macOS 10.15+, or Linux (Ubuntu 18.04+)
- **Browser Support**: Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Edge 90+, Safari 14+
- **Network**: Internet connection for desktop-server communication
- **Memory**: Minimum 4GB RAM (8GB recommended)
- **Storage**: 1GB free space for application and test data

### Account Setup
1. **Register for UITrace**: Create account at https://uitrace.dev/signup
2. **Choose Authentication Method**:
   - **OAuth2**: Login with Google, GitHub, or Microsoft account
   - **Local Account**: Create username/password pair
3. **Verify Email**: Check inbox for verification email
4. **Join or Create Team**: Join existing team or create your own

## Installation

### Desktop Client
1. **Download UITrace Desktop**:
   - Windows: `UITrace-Setup-x.x.x.exe`
   - macOS: `UITrace-x.x.x.dmg`
   - Linux: `uitrace-x.x.x.AppImage` or `uitrace-x.x.x.deb`

2. **Install Application**:
   ```bash
   # Windows
   Double-click UITrace-Setup-x.x.x.exe and follow installer

   # macOS
   Open UITrace-x.x.x.dmg and drag to Applications folder

   # Linux (AppImage)
   chmod +x uitrace-x.x.x.AppImage
   ./uitrace-x.x.x.AppImage

   # Linux (Deb)
   sudo dpkg -i uitrace-x.x.x.deb
   ```

3. **Launch Application**:
   - Windows: Start Menu → UITrace
   - macOS: Applications → UITrace
   - Linux: Applications → UITrace or run `uitrace`

4. **Sign In**: Use your credentials to authenticate desktop client

### Browser Extension (Optional)
For enhanced recording capabilities:
1. **Install Browser Extension**:
   - Chrome Web Store: "UITrace Recorder"
   - Firefox Add-ons: "UITrace Recorder"
   - Edge Add-ons: "UITrace Recorder"

2. **Enable Extension**: Grant permissions for the extension to access web pages

## Your First Test Script

### Step 1: Create Project
1. **Open UITrace Desktop**
2. **Click "New Project"**
3. **Fill Project Details**:
   - **Name**: "My First Test Suite"
   - **Description**: "Getting started with UITrace"
   - **Team**: Select your team
   - **Data Retention**: 12 months (default)
4. **Click "Create Project"**

### Step 2: Record Test Script
1. **Click "New Script"**
2. **Enter Script Name**: "Login Test"
3. **Click "Start Recording"**
4. **Browser opens** - perform these actions:
   - Navigate to your test website
   - Click login button
   - Enter username: `test@example.com`
   - Enter password: `password123`
   - Click submit button
   - Wait for page to load
   - Verify successful login message
5. **Stop Recording**: Click "Stop" in UITrace toolbar
6. **Review Script**: Check generated steps and selectors

### Step 3: Edit and Enhance Script
1. **Review Generated Steps**:
   ```json
   [
     {
       "stepId": 1,
       "name": "Navigate to login page",
       "action": "navigate",
       "value": "https://example.com/login",
       "timeoutSeconds": 10,
       "selectors": [
         {"type": "url", "value": "https://example.com/login"}
       ]
     },
     {
       "stepId": 2,
       "name": "Enter username",
       "action": "type",
       "value": "test@example.com",
       "timeoutSeconds": 5,
       "selectors": [
         {"type": "id", "value": "username"},
         {"type": "css", "value": "input[type='email']"},
         {"type": "xpath", "value": "//input[@name='username']"}
       ]
     }
   ]
   ```

2. **Improve Selectors**:
   - Add data-test attributes to application if possible
   - Verify fallback selectors are appropriate
   - Adjust timeout values for network conditions

3. **Add Assertions**:
   ```json
   {
     "stepId": 5,
     "name": "Verify login success",
     "action": "assert_text",
     "expectedValue": "Welcome back",
     "timeoutSeconds": 5,
     "selectors": [
       {"type": "css", "value": ".welcome-message"}
     ]
   }
   ```

4. **Add Visual Validation** (optional):
   ```json
   {
     "stepId": 6,
     "name": "Capture dashboard screenshot",
     "action": "screenshot",
     "timeoutSeconds": 2,
     "baselineName": "dashboard-layout"
   }
   ```

### Step 4: Save Script
1. **Click "Save Script"**
2. **Enter Version Notes**: "Initial login test with visual validation"
3. **Script Status**: Change from "Draft" to "Ready"
4. **Click "Save"**

## Running Your First Test

### Execute Single Test
1. **Select Script**: Click on your saved script
2. **Choose Browser**: Chrome (default), Firefox, or Edge
3. **Click "Run Test"**
4. **Monitor Execution**:
   - Real-time step execution status
   - Progress bar and timing information
   - Error messages if any step fails

### Test Results

   - **Step Details**: Each step with timing and status
   - **Screenshots**: Before/after images for visual steps
   - **Error Logs**: Detailed information for failed steps

2. **Visual Comparison** (if configured):
   - Similarity score percentage
   - Highlighted differences from baseline
   - Option to accept new baseline

## Data-Driven Testing

### Prepare Test Data
1. **Create CSV File** (`test_users.csv`):
   ```csv
   username,password,expected_role
   alice@example.com,password123,admin
   bob@example.com,secure456,user
   charlie@example.com,secret789,moderator
   ```

2. **Upload Data File**:
   - Click "Data Files" tab
   - Click "Upload File"
   - Select `test_users.csv`
   - Configure column types and validation

### Configure Data-Driven Script
1. **Edit Script**: Open your login test script
2. **Replace Hardcoded Values**:
   ```json
   {
     "stepId": 2,
     "name": "Enter username",
     "action": "type",
     "value": "${username}",  // Use variable from CSV
     "timeoutSeconds": 5,
     "selectors": [...]
   },
   {
     "stepId": 3,
     "name": "Enter password",
     "action": "type",
     "value": "${password}",  // Use variable from CSV
     "timeoutSeconds": 5,
     "selectors": [...]
   }
   ```

3. **Link Data File**:
   - Click "Data Integration" tab
   - Select uploaded CSV file
   - Map variables to column names
   - Verify data types and validation

### Run Data-Driven Test
1. **Select Execution Mode**: "Data-Driven"
2. **Choose Data File**: Your uploaded CSV
3. **Click "Run Test"**
4. **Monitor Results**:
   - 3 independent test cases execute
   - Each case isolated with fresh browser state
   - Combined report with individual case results

2. **Select Script**: Choose script to share
3. **Click "Share"**:

### Script Recording
- **Start Simple**: Record basic flow first, then enhance
- **Use Meaningful Names**: Descriptive step names for maintainability
- **Appropriate Timeouts**: Set realistic values for network conditions
- **Multiple Selectors**: Ensure robust fallback strategies

### Test Organization
- **Modular Scripts**: Break large tests into smaller, reusable scripts
- **Consistent Naming**: Use naming conventions for scripts and projects

- **Thresholds**: Adjust similarity thresholds based on application tolerance
- **Regular Updates**: Update baselines when application design changes

- **Cause**: UI elements changed or page not fully loaded
- **Solutions**:

  - Add additional selector strategies

  - Add wait steps for dynamic content

# Implementation Plan: UITrace Platform

**Branch**: `001-uitrace-platform` | **Date**: 2025-11-27 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-uitrace-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is filled in by the `/speckit.plan` command. See `.specify/templates/commands/plan.md` for the execution workflow.

## Summary

UITrace is a comprehensive UI automation testing platform with dual architecture: Rust/Tauri desktop client for high-performance test execution and Python/FastAPI server for collaboration and data management. The platform will enable QA engineers to record, edit, and execute test scripts with intelligent fault tolerance, data-driven testing, visual validation, and centralized team collaboration features. The technical approach follows Test-First development principles and leverages modern web technologies to achieve sub-500ms execution times with 98% reliability on slightly modified UIs.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Rust 1.75+ (Desktop), Python 3.11+ (Server), TypeScript 5.0+ (Frontend)
**Primary Dependencies**: Tauri 2.0, Tokio async runtime, Thirtyfour WebDriver, Vue 3, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL
**Storage**: PostgreSQL for structured data, file system for test scripts and screenshots, Redis for session caching
**Testing**: Cargo test (unit), WebDriver testing (integration), pytest (server API), end-to-end browser testing
**Target Platform**: Desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux), Web server (Linux containers), Browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
**Project Type**: Multi-component web application with desktop client and server backend
**Performance Goals**: Sub-500ms step execution, <2s API response times, 98% test reliability, 50+ concurrent users
**Constraints**: Cross-browser compatibility, offline script editing capability, automatic data cleanup per retention policies, 99.5% uptime during business hours
**Scale/Scope**: Support 1000+ concurrent test executions, 10k+ test scripts, 100+ user teams, enterprise-grade security and compliance

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Constitution Compliance Status

✅ **I. Client-Server Architecture**: Dual-component architecture confirmed (Rust/Tauri desktop + Python/FastAPI server)
✅ **II. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)**: TDD approach specified with comprehensive testing strategy

## Task Generation Rules

**CRITICAL**: Tasks MUST be organized by user story to enable independent implementation and testing.

**Tests are OPTIONAL**: Only generate test tasks if explicitly requested in the feature specification or if user requests TDD approach.

### Checklist Format (REQUIRED)

Every task MUST strictly follow this format:

```text
- [ ] [TaskID] [P?] [Story?] Description with file path
```

**Format Components**:

1. **Checkbox**: ALWAYS start with `- [ ]` (markdown checkbox)
2. **Task ID**: Sequential number (T001, T002, T003...) in execution order
3. **[P] marker**: Include ONLY if task is parallelizable (different files, no dependencies on incomplete tasks)
4. **[Story] label**: REQUIRED for user story phase tasks only
   - Format: [US1], [US2], [US3], etc. (maps to user stories from spec.md)
   - Setup phase: NO story label
   - Foundational phase: NO story label  
   - User Story phases: MUST have story label
   - Polish phase: NO story label
5. **Description**: Clear action with exact file path

**Examples**:

- ✅ CORRECT: `- [ ] T001 Create project structure per implementation plan`
- ✅ CORRECT: `- [ ] T005 [P] Implement authentication middleware in src/middleware/auth.py`
- ✅ CORRECT: `- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Create User model in src/models/user.py`
- ✅ CORRECT: `- [ ] T014 [US1] Implement UserService in src/services/user_service.py`
- ❌ WRONG: `- [ ] Create User model` (missing ID and Story label)
- ❌ WRONG: `T001 [US1] Create model` (missing checkbox)
- ❌ WRONG: `- [ ] [US1] Create User model` (missing Task ID)
- ❌ WRONG: `- [ ] T001 [US1] Create model` (missing file path)

1. **From User Stories (spec.md)** - PRIMARY ORGANIZATION:
   - Each user story (P1, P2, P3...) gets its own phase
   - Map all related components to their story:
     - Models needed for that story
     - Services needed for that story
     - Endpoints/UI needed for that story
     - If tests requested: Tests specific to that story
   - Mark story dependencies (most stories should be independent)

2. **From Contracts**:
   - Map each contract/endpoint → to the user story it serves
   - If tests requested: Each contract → contract test task [P] before implementation in that story's phase

3. **From Data Model**:
   - Map each entity to the user story(ies) that need it
   - If entity serves multiple stories: Put in earliest story or Setup phase
   - Relationships → service layer tasks in appropriate story phase

4. **From Setup/Infrastructure**:
   - Shared infrastructure → Setup phase (Phase 1)
   - Foundational/blocking tasks → Foundational phase (Phase 2)
   - Story-specific setup → within that story's phase

### Phase Structure

- **Phase 1**: Setup (project initialization)
- **Phase 2**: Foundational (blocking prerequisites - MUST complete before user stories)
- **Phase 3+**: User Stories in priority order (P1, P2, P3...)

UITrace is a comprehensive UI automation testing platform with dual architecture: Rust/Tauri desktop client for high-performance test execution and Python/FastAPI server for collaboration and data management. The platform will enable QA engineers to record, edit, and execute test scripts with intelligent fault tolerance, data-driven testing, visual validation, and centralized team collaboration features. The technical approach follows Test-First development principles and leverages modern web technologies to achieve sub-500ms execution times with 98% reliability on slightly modified UIs.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Rust 1.75+ (Desktop), Python 3.11+ (Server), TypeScript 5.0+ (Frontend)
**Primary Dependencies**: Tauri 2.0, Tokio async runtime, Thirtyfour WebDriver, Vue 3, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL
**Storage**: PostgreSQL for structured data, file system for test scripts and screenshots, Redis for session caching
**Testing**: Cargo test (unit), WebDriver testing (integration), pytest (server API), end-to-end browser testing
**Target Platform**: Desktop (Windows, macOS, Linux), Web server (Linux containers), Browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
**Project Type**: Multi-component web application with desktop client and server backend
**Performance Goals**: Sub-500ms step execution, <2s API response times, 98% test reliability, 50+ concurrent users
**Constraints**: Cross-browser compatibility, offline script editing capability, automatic data cleanup per retention policies, 99.5% uptime during business hours
**Scale/Scope**: Support 1000+ concurrent test executions, 10k+ test scripts, 100+ user teams, enterprise-grade security and compliance

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Constitution Compliance Status

✅ **I. Client-Server Architecture**: Dual-component architecture confirmed (Rust/Tauri desktop + Python/FastAPI server)
✅ **II. Test-First (NON-NEGOTIABLE)**: TDD approach specified with comprehensive testing strategy
✅ **III. Fault-Tolerant Execution**: Multi-selector strategies with intelligent retry mechanisms included
✅ **IV. Data-Driven Testing (DDT)**: CSV/Excel parameterization with `${variable}` syntax specified
✅ **V. Performance and Reliability**: Sub-500ms execution times and 98% reliability requirements defined

### Architecture Standards Compliance

✅ **Technology Stack**: Uses Rust/Tauri, Python/FastAPI, PostgreSQL as required by constitution
✅ **API Design**: RESTful APIs with JSON data transmission specified

### User Story 1 - Script Recording and Editing (Priority: P1)

As a QA engineer, I want to record user interactions with web applications so that I can create automated test scripts without manual coding.

**Why this priority**: Core functionality that enables test automation - without recording capability, the entire platform has no value proposition.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by recording a simple user journey (login + search + logout) and validating that the generated script contains all steps with appropriate selectors and timing.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a user has launched the UITrace desktop application and navigated to a web page, **When** they click "Start Recording" and perform user actions (clicks, typing, navigation), **Then** the system captures each action with at least 3 alternative selectors (ID, CSS, XPath) and saves them as a JSON script.
2. **Given** a user has recorded a script, **When** they open the script editor, **Then** they can modify step descriptions, adjust timeout values, add/remove steps, and change selector priorities.
3. **Given** a user has saved a script, **When** they reopen the script later, **Then** all steps, selectors, and metadata are preserved and editable.

---

### User Story 2 - Fault-Tolerant Script Execution (Priority: P1)

As a QA engineer, I want to execute recorded test scripts with automatic error recovery so that tests continue running even when UI elements change or page loads are slow.

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Fault-Tolerant Script Execution (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Execute recorded test scripts with automatic error recovery using multiple selector strategies

## Phase 5: User Story 3 - Data-Driven Testing (Priority: P2)

## Phase 6: User Story 4 - Visual Validation and Comparison (Priority: P2)

## Phase 7: User Story 5 - Centralized Script and Result Management (Priority: P3)

**Goal**: Provide web-based centralized management for test scripts and execution results with team collaboration

**Independent Test**: Can upload scripts through web interface and view execution results in centralized dashboard

**Checkpoint**: All user stories should now be independently functional - complete end-to-end UI testing platform

## Phase 8: Cross-Cutting Concerns & Integration

**Purpose**: Integration between components and performance optimization across all features

- [ ] T070 [P] [Integration] Integrate desktop client with server API in desktop/src/services/
- [ ] T071 [P] [Integration] Implement offline-first architecture for desktop client in desktop/src/
- [ ] T072 [P] [Integration] Add real-time sync between desktop and server components
- [ ] T073 [P] [Integration] Optimize performance for sub-500ms step execution targets
- [ ] T074 [Integration] Implement comprehensive error handling and user feedback across components
- [ ] T075 [P] [Integration] Add automated data cleanup based on retention policies in server/
- [ ] T076 [P] [Integration] Create comprehensive audit logging system in server/
- [ ] T077 [P] [Integration] Implement security hardening (input validation, encryption) in both components
- [ ] T078 [Integration] Add cross-browser compatibility testing and optimization
- [ ] T079 [Integration] Create build and deployment scripts for all components
- [ ] T080 [Integration] Implement CI/CD pipeline configuration files
- [ ] T081 [Integration] Create comprehensive documentation (API docs, user guides, development docs)
- [ ] T082 [Integration] Add application monitoring and health checks
- [ ] T083 [Integration] Performance testing and optimization
- [ ] T084 [Integration] Security testing and vulnerability assessment
- [ ] T085 [Integration] Create deployment guides and Docker containerization

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - can start immediately
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup completion - BLOCKS all user stories
- **User Stories (Phases 3-7)**: All depend on Foundational phase completion
  - User stories can be implemented in parallel by different team members
  - Stories follow priority order: P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5
- **Integration (Phase 8)**: Depends on all desired user stories being complete

### User Story Dependencies

- **User Story 1 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **User Story 2 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format
- **User Story 3 (P2)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format and User Story 2 for execution engine
- **User Story 4 (P2)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 2 for execution engine integration
- **User Story 5 (P3)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format and User Story 2 for result structure

### Within Each User Story

- Tests (if included) MUST be written and FAIL before implementation
- Models before services
- Services before endpoints/UI
- Core implementation before integration
- Story complete before moving to next priority

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] can run in parallel across desktop/server/frontend components
- All Foundational tasks marked [P] can run in parallel (within Phase 2)
- Once Foundational phase completes, all user stories can start in parallel (if team capacity allows)
- All tasks marked [P] within a user story can run in parallel
- Different user stories can be worked on in parallel by different team members
- Integration tasks in Phase 8 can run in parallel for cross-cutting concerns

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1 & 2

```bash
# Launch all implementation tasks for User Story 1 together:
Task: "Setup Tauri application structure in desktop/src/"
Task: "Create browser extension interface in desktop/src/recorder/"
Task: "Implement DOM event capture system in desktop/src/recorder/"

# Launch all implementation tasks for User Story 2 in parallel:
Task: "Implement WebDriver client wrapper in desktop/src/executor/"
Task: "Create intelligent retry mechanism in desktop/src/executor/"
Task: "Implement multi-selector fallback strategy in desktop/src/executor/"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Stories 1 + 2)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL - blocks all stories)
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (Script Recording and Editing)
4. Complete Phase 4: User Story 2 (Fault-Tolerant Execution)
5. **STOP AND VALIDATE**: Test core recording and execution functionality independently
6. Deploy/demo basic UI automation capabilities

### Incremental Delivery

1. Complete Setup + Foundational → Foundation ready
2. Add User Story 1 → Record and edit test scripts (MVP core functionality)
3. Add User Story 2 → Execute scripts with fault tolerance (MVP reliability)
4. Add User Story 3 → Data-driven testing (Enhanced automation)
5. Add User Story 4 → Visual validation (Complete testing coverage)
6. Add User Story 5 → Centralized management (Team collaboration)
7. Complete Phase 8: Integration → Production-ready platform

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers:

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together
2. Once Foundational is done:
   - Developer A: User Story 1 (Recording & Editing)
   - Developer B: User Story 2 (Execution Engine)
   - Developer C: User Story 5 (Server APIs)
3. Stories complete and integrate independently
4. Integration phase combines all components

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no dependencies, can run in parallel
- [Story] label maps task to specific user story for traceability
- Each user story should be independently completable and testable
- Tasks are organized to enable incremental delivery of working functionality
- Verify tasks can be completed by developers without additional context
- Stop at each checkpoint to validate story independently
- Focus on core functionality first, then add advanced features
- Multi-component architecture allows parallel development across Rust, Python, and Vue.js teams

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup completion - BLOCKS all user stories
- **User Stories (Phases 3-7)**: All depend on Foundational phase completion
  - User stories can be implemented in parallel by different team members
  - Stories follow priority order: P1 → P2 → P3 → P4 → P5
- **Integration (Phase 8)**: Depends on all desired user stories being complete

### User Story Dependencies

- **User Story 1 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **User Story 2 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format
- **User Story 3 (P2)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format and User Story 2 for execution engine
- **User Story 4 (P2)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 2 for execution engine integration
- **User Story 5 (P3)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - Depends on User Story 1 for script format and User Story 2 for result structure

### Within Each User Story

- Tests (if included) MUST be written and FAIL before implementation
- Models before services
- Services before endpoints/UI
- Core implementation before integration
- Story complete before moving to next priority

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] can run in parallel across desktop/server/frontend components
- All Foundational tasks marked [P] can run in parallel (within Phase 2)
- Once Foundational phase completes, all user stories can start in parallel (if team capacity allows)
- All tasks marked [P] within a user story can run in parallel
- Different user stories can be worked on in parallel by different team members
- Integration tasks in Phase 8 can run in parallel for cross-cutting concerns

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1 & 2

```bash

Task: "Setup Tauri application structure in desktop/src/"
Task: "Create browser extension interface in desktop/src/recorder/"
Task: "Implement DOM event capture system in desktop/src/recorder/"

# Launch all implementation tasks for User Story 2 in parallel:
Task: "Implement WebDriver client wrapper in desktop/src/executor/"
Task: "Create intelligent retry mechanism in desktop/src/executor/"
Task: "Implement multi-selector fallback strategy in desktop/src/executor/"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Stories 1 + 2)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL - blocks all stories)
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (Script Recording and Editing)
4. Complete Phase 4: User Story 2 (Fault-Tolerant Execution)
5. **STOP AND VALIDATE**: Test core recording and execution functionality independently
6. Deploy/demo basic UI automation capabilities

### Incremental Delivery

1. Complete Setup + Foundational → Foundation ready
2. Add User Story 1 → Record and edit test scripts (MVP core functionality)
3. Add User Story 2 → Execute scripts with fault tolerance (MVP reliability)
4. Add User Story 3 → Data-driven testing (Enhanced automation)
5. Add User Story 4 → Visual validation (Complete testing coverage)
6. Add User Story 5 → Centralized management (Team collaboration)
7. Complete Phase 8: Integration → Production-ready platform

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers:

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together
2. Once Foundational is done:
   - Developer A: User Story 1 (Recording & Editing)
   - Developer B: User Story 2 (Execution Engine)
   - Developer C: User Story 5 (Server APIs)
3. Stories complete and integrate independently
4. Integration phase combines all components

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no dependencies, can run in parallel
- [Story] label maps task to specific user story for traceability
- Each user story should be independently completable and testable
- Tasks are organized to enable incremental delivery of working functionality
- Verify tasks can be completed by developers without additional context
- Stop at each checkpoint to validate story independently
- Focus on core functionality first, then add advanced features
- Multi-component architecture allows parallel development across Rust, Python, and Vue.js teams

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Project initialization and basic structure for multi-component application

- [ ] T001 [P] [Setup] Create project structure per implementation plan
- [ ] T002 [P] [Setup] Initialize Rust desktop project with Tauri dependencies
- [ ] T003 [P] [Setup] Initialize Python server project with FastAPI dependencies
- [ ] T004 [P] [Setup] Initialize Vue 3 frontend project for desktop UI
- [ ] T005 [P] [Setup] Configure linting and formatting tools for all components

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Core infrastructure that MUST be complete before ANY user story can be implemented

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete

- [ ] T006 [Setup] Setup PostgreSQL database with migration system in server/
- [ ] T007 [Setup] Setup Redis caching layer in server/ for session management
- [ ] T008 [Setup] Configure authentication service (OAuth2 + local accounts) in server/
- [ ] T009 [P] Setup database models and schemas in server/models/
- [ ] T010 [Setup] Setup FastAPI routing and middleware structure in server/
- [ ] T011 [P] Configure error handling and logging infrastructure in server/
- [ ] T012 [P] Setup environment configuration management for all components
- [ ] T013 [Setup] Configure TypeScript types and shared schemas in shared/

**Checkpoint**: Foundation ready - desktop client and server components can now be implemented in parallel

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - Script Recording and Editing (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Enable users to record web interactions and edit test scripts without manual coding

**Independent Test**: Desktop client can record a simple journey (login + search + logout) and generate a valid JSON script with multiple selector strategies

### Tests for User Story 1 (Not Requested - focusing on implementation)

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T014 [US1] [Setup] Setup Tauri application structure in desktop/src/
- [ ] T015 [P] [US1] Create browser extension interface in desktop/src/recorder/
- [ ] T016 [P] [US1] Implement DOM event capture system for click, type, navigation events in desktop/src/recorder/
- [ ] T017 [US1] Generate multiple selector strategies (ID, CSS, XPath) for captured elements in desktop/src/recorder/
- [ ] T018 [P] [US1] Create JSON script format and serialization logic in desktop/src/models/
- [ ] T019 [US1] Implement WebDriver-based recording fallback in desktop/src/recorder/
- [ ] T020 [US1] Create script editor Vue component in desktop/src-ui/components/ScriptEditor.vue
- [ ] T021 [US1] Implement script loading and saving functionality in desktop/src/services/script_service.rs
- [ ] T022 [US1] Add selector editing and priority adjustment in script editor in desktop/src-ui/
- [ ] T023 [US1] Create script metadata management (name, description, version) in desktop/src/
- [ ] T024 [US1] Test recording functionality with sample web application

**Checkpoint**: At this point, User Story 1 should be fully functional - users can record and edit basic test scripts

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Fault-Tolerant Script Execution (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: Execute recorded test scripts with automatic error recovery using multiple selector strategies

**Independent Test**: Can execute a script against a slightly modified UI and succeed through automatic selector fallback

### Tests for User Story 2 (Not Requested - focusing on implementation)

- [ ] T029 [US2] Create element interaction handlers (click, type, navigate) in desktop/src/executor/
- [ ] T030 [US2] Implement progress tracking and status reporting in desktop/src/executor/
- [ ] T031 [US2] Add execution control (pause, resume, stop) in desktop/src/executor/
- [ ] T032 [US2] Create execution results capture (timing, success/failure) in desktop/src/executor/
- [ ] T033 [US2] Implement error logging and debugging information in desktop/src/executor/
- [ ] T034 [US2] Create execution UI component in desktop/src-ui/components/ExecutionMonitor.vue
- [ ] T035 [US2] Test fault tolerance with modified UI elements
